T: Onboard to the project: read the Pre-Discovery Kickoff and Plan and the master plan workbook (your 12 deliverables, 160 hours and sessions), and open the project workspace (shared folder, Figma or Miro, file naming, participant codes).
Read the documents we already have: business case, Connected Workforce pitch and Slalom Connect! 2026. Note what HT asked for and what Slalom proposed.

Onboard to SharePoint: learn the building blocks (site types, templates, web parts, navigation, audiences, search, Viva Connections). Once access is granted, tour HT’s intranet and capture screenshots, navigation and brand guidelines. Check design-tool, VDI and access limits; log gaps in RAIDD.

Agree cadence and ways of working with the team (stand-up, weekly status, focus plans, file locations, review and decision log). Draft the one-page XD workplan with co-facilitation roles. Note the generative AI rule: approved tools only.

Chase the discovery files: ask the Programme Owner for all outputs and any existing personas, set up the inventory and request list, and agree plan B with the Engagement Lead if files are not shared by Day 1.
Draft persona strawmen and journey assumptions from the documents we have (no existing personas are expected) and set up the assumptions log in the Personas tab. Nothing counts as evidence yet.
Plan the research with the Change Manager: research plan one-pager, interview screener and consent note, and the works council and HR questions (route and lead time).
Confirm with HT: the in-person design session room and the 4 to 6 stakeholders with decision authority. Hold the diaries.

Draft the workshop packs from the assumptions: persona workshop (#8), and the design session agenda and invite. Mark what depends on files not yet received. Check which Connect! assets can seed prototype v0.
Send the Week 1 focus plan. Walk through the Before Day 1 readiness list with the Engagement Lead (access, discovery files, participants, rooms) and decide whether plan B starts on Monday.

Attend the Slalom internal kickoff and the programme kickoff (#1, 90 min). Ask: who are the 4 to 6 design stakeholders, who owns brand, what are the frontline access limits, what are the tool limits? Also ask whether any personas, segments or employee research exist anywhere (HR, comms, IT, earlier intranet work).
Contribute to the Ways of Working canvas: propose UX agreements (drafts 48 hours ahead, feedback within 24 hours, decide in the room).
Re-validate assumptions with the Programme Owner: are discovery outputs complete? Log missing inputs in the gaps log.
Lock names and diaries for design session attendees. Send the invite and the pre-read request.
Send recruitment requests with the screener. Confirm the first interview slots with the Change Lead.
Set your routine: daily 15-minute stand-up, weekly status input to the Engagement Lead, a focus plan at the start of each week, meeting notes within 24 hours, peer review before anything is issued.
Ask the Programme Owner the open questions you own (Dependencies tab): must-haves versus later waves, Phase 1 languages, what is validated versus draft, SME availability.
Check the inventory against what has arrived since Friday. Decide plan A (files received) or plan B and tell the Engagement Lead and Programme Owner today.

Give the Change Manager your questions for the sponsor and priority-lead interviews (#4): vision for the experience, which employee groups matter most and who is hardest to reach, frontline priorities, appetite for tailoring, brand. Use the interview guide.
Join the vision, objectives and value framework session (#3). Add UX success measures: findability, task success, adoption by persona.
After the interviews, note how much tailoring the sponsor expects, using the short seven-question scorecard on the Standard vs tailored tab. Keep it to ten minutes.
Read the discovery outputs that have arrived and fill the inventory sheet. For anything still missing, add it to the gaps log and follow plan B.

Run the HT Discovery deep dive, session 1 of 2 (#7, 90 min): walk each output, mark what is validated, stale or missing. If files are still missing, run it as a walkthrough where the Programme Owner and SMEs present what exists.
Run deep dive session 2 of 2 (#7, 90 min): turn findings into the draft consolidated backlog (ID, source, persona (draft), MoSCoW, confidence) and the gaps log.

Run first interviews with group B (team leader or site manager) and group F (content owner) if participants are confirmed. Use them to elicit personas: a day in the life, what information they need, what they do today.
Update the persona strawmen with deep-dive findings and anything persona-relevant in the files (surveys, segments, comms audiences). Mark which have strong and which thin evidence.
Check the backlog tool (Jira, Planner or Azure DevOps, decision DE3) is ready. Put your deliverables and the draft backlog items in it.
Confirm accessibility, language and inclusion requirements with the Programme Owner and note them as design principles.
Facilitate the Persona creation and journey workshop (#8, 90 min) with the Change Manager: build the personas with HT from the strawmen, then draft journey assumptions. See the Workshops tab.
Run the Frontline access model and Phase-1 languages decision (#9, 60 min). Bring options and the design impact of each; log decisions the same day.
Get the outcome of the works council and HR alignment (#10): route, lead time, what is allowed for interviews and usability tests.
Turn the workshop output into persona v1 and the journey assumptions. Record the evidence level for each, which personas are primary for Phase 1, and what still needs validating.
Hold more interviews this week: groups C, D and E (desk, remote, new starter). Complete the capture sheet within 30 minutes of each. Use them to test and sharpen persona v1.
Give the Engagement Lead your readiness view for Risk Gate 1 (#11): access, participants, inputs, attendees, risks.
Finalise the design session agenda, roles and room plan. Dry-run Day 1 and Day 2 for 60 minutes with the Change Manager, Solution Architect and Engagement Lead.

Send the pre-read to design session attendees so Day 1 starts with reactions, not reading: vision draft, persona v1 and journey assumptions (built in Week 1, as no earlier personas exist), key quotes, what we heard.

With the Change Manager and Solution Architect (who own facilitation materials), print and pack the kit: journey wall, requirement cards, voting dots, story templates, parking lot, reference gallery and IA cards. Confirm photo and recording consent.
Log XD risks and decisions in RAIDD and update weekly status.
Send your Week 2 focus plan on a page.
Update the Deliverables tab: status, % complete and health for each deliverable. Flag anything at risk to the Engagement Lead.
Add your 12 deliverables to the Artefact Register (the Engagement Lead keeps it; each lead keeps their own entries current).

Prepare the Day 1 design block kit: reference gallery (4 to 5 cleared intranet references plus Connect! patterns, 3 screens each, green and red dots) and the IA card-sort deck (about 25 cards from the Must requirements and top moments, blanks, 5 to 6 candidate headers).
Send persona v1 and the journey assumptions to the Product Owner and SMEs for written comment by Mon 16 Nov 09:00 (also in the pre-read). Log their comments in the assumptions log.
Set up the room 60 minutes before start: journey wall, persona cards, evidence wall, requirement card wall, reference gallery, sketch stations, parking lot.

Facilitate design session Day 1 (#12) with the Change Manager, blocks 1 to 4: purpose, vision and success; personas and journeys; requirements in context (with the Solution Architect); design studio with the reference vote, sketching, IA card sort and one concept.
Photograph and transcribe all boards the same evening. Write the Day 1 playback and the Day 2 plan, including open questions and the parking lot.
Start prototype v0 on Monday evening: home, navigation, department site, news, search and one frontline surface. Reuse Connect! templates.
In block 2, record for each persona and journey whether HT confirmed, changed or rejected it. Update the status in the Personas tab the same evening.

Facilitate design session Day 2 (#13) with the Change Manager: refine the concept and scope, shape epics and user stories (with the Solution Architect), rank and sequence the backlog, then readiness, sign-off and next steps.
In block 5.3 (in, out, later board) tag each item standard or tailored and record where stakeholders disagree. No separate exercise.
Get backlog sign-off from the Programme Owner in the room in block 8.2 (fist-of-five consent). Log decisions the same day.
Continue the prototype build. Define test scope: 4 to 5 core tasks per persona group.
Draft the directional IA and site map from the card sort and Day 1 decisions (due Thu 19 Nov): top navigation, department template, search facets and one frontline entry point.
After the backlog sign-off, send HT the signed-off backlog and decision log. Record the pack-shared date on the Deliverables tab; formal acceptance is due in 5 business days.
Contribute to Transformation narrative and engagement (#14, 90 min): personas, journeys and quotes the narrative can use.
Give input to Content assessment and ownership (#16): content types, templates needed, IA implications. The schedule does not list you, so ask to be invited or brief the Solution Architect.
Write the usability test plan, script, task cards, observer sheet, consent and severity scale. Confirm 4 participants (2 desk, 2 frontline).
Finish click-through prototype v1 for testing: desktop, mobile and a frontline mock (kiosk or shared device). Check links and content in the local language.
Pilot the test with a colleague. Fix tasks and broken prototype paths.
Produce low-fidelity wireframes for the agreed page types (home, department site, news, search, one frontline surface) in desktop and mobile. Due Thu 19 Nov.
Run usability round 1 (#17, 4 × 60 min, desk and frontline). Debrief after each session and log issues with severity.
Synthesise the same evening: top issues, what to change before sign-off, whether round 2 is needed.
Finish the site map and wireframes. Check feasibility with the Solution Architect and adoption fit with the Change Manager.
Draft two to three branding and theme directions (colour, type, imagery, tone) from the Day 1 design preference map and the HT brand guidelines. Due Tue 24 Nov for design sign-off.
Update the prototype for the highest-severity issues before the sign-off.
Present the prototype and findings at Prototype sign-off (#18, 60 to 90 min). Capture change requests and get sign-off from the Programme Owner and design stakeholders.
Decide with the Change Manager whether round 2 is needed on Mon 23 Nov. Confirm 2 participants.
Send the Week 3 focus plan and update RAIDD.
After the prototype sign-off, send HT the prototype link and record the pack-shared date on the Deliverables tab (5 business days to accept).
Run usability round 2 (#20, 2 × 60 min) if needed, on changed flows only.
Prepare the Design sign-off pack: personas, journeys, IA map, prototype link, branding direction, findings, UX success measures.
Write a half-page view of where HT wants standard Connect! and where tailoring is justified, from the scorecard, interviews and design session. No full profile needed.
Analyse the usability findings and refine the IA, wireframes and prototype (deliverable due Tue 24 Nov).
Run Design sign-off (#21, 60 min): present, record decisions, get Programme Owner and Product Owner sign-off.
Give input to Integration discovery and AI readiness (#22): assistant conversation flows, expectations, guardrails, what users see when AI cannot answer. Ask to be invited.
Share the half-page view with the Solution Architect to align the OOTB-versus-custom recommendation.
After the Design sign-off, send HT the design pack and record the pack-shared date on the Deliverables tab (5 business days to accept).
Join the Change and Adoption plus comms review (#23): link journeys to adoption touchpoints; check success measures are measurable.
If asked, give UX input to the AI governance, ARB and security review (#24): user-facing AI behaviour, data shown, consent text.
Check the Architecture sign-off (#25) for UX-critical custom items. Flag any that conflict with the signed-off design.
Start assembling the Design section of the Discovery outcome.
Finish the draft design outcome: personas, journeys, IA and site map, wireframes, prototype, findings, branding, success measures and the standard-versus-tailored view.
Share the draft with the Engagement Lead for review before Week 4.
Update the Deliverables tab and send your Week 4 focus plan on a page.
Consolidate XD outputs into the Discovery outcome. Check consistency with the architecture and change sign-offs.
Prepare XD input to the costed plan: design effort per delivery wave (templates, personas, languages, branding).
Ask to join Delivery planning and wave options (#27). Propose waves by persona and surface and show the design effort for each wave.
Prepare your playback segment: 10 to 15 minutes, prototype demo, three quotes per persona.
Present at Playback (#28): design, findings and the way forward. Log any change requests through change control.
Hand off: organise the repository, prototype files, anonymised research data, open questions and research debt.
Confirm acceptance criteria for design deliverables with the Programme Owner before Friday.
Final acceptance (#29): confirm design deliverables accepted.
Hold a short retro on the research approach. Record what to repeat in Delivery.

React to the strawmen and fill the gaps

Persona v1 cards with evidence markers

Pairs map three moments per top persona: steps, channel, device, pain, workaround. Mark each step as known, assumed or unknown

Read back decisions; preview async comment and Day 1

Ask “who is missing?” before voting, especially frontline groups and the roughly 2,000 employees without a PC.

Pairs brainwrite: “It is one year after launch. What is true for employees?” Cluster on the wall into 3 to 5 success measures, including adoption and findability

Small groups each take one draft persona (built with HT in #8 and sharpened by interviews; there is no earlier persona set) and react: what rings true, what is missing, who is not represented. HT confirms, changes or rejects each one

Journey mapping on the wall, starting from the journey assumptions drafted in #8. Groups map one priority journey end to end: steps, tools used, feelings, and where people leave to find help elsewhere. Mark each step as confirmed or still an assumption
Dot-vote on pain points and opportunities, then plenary to agree the top moments. HT stakeholders challenge and add what only they know
Requirement cards placed against the journey map from Block 2. Show where each need lands and which moments have no requirement yet

Must, Should, Could sorting, then a plenary check against the success measures from Block 1. Agree what shapes the first release

Design preference map and 4 to 5 principles (look, tone, density, imagery)
Design studio. Mixed HT and Slalom pairs sketch how the intelligent home could look and behave, using the top moments, the Must requirements and the design principles as the brief
Gallery walk with sticky-note feedback (like, wish, what if), then a short plenary to pull out the strongest ideas and open questions

Hybrid card sort with about 25 cards (content types and functions from the Must requirements and the sketches) and 5 to 6 candidate headers. Three mixed groups sort, rename headers and add missing cards (10 min), compare results (10 min), agree the top navigation, department template and search facets (10 min)
Draft IA: top navigation, department template, facets
Facilitated plenary to agree one concept, the draft IA and site map, and a playback of what Day 1 decided
One concept, draft IA and site map, Day 1 playback, open questions for Day 2
tips: Agenda follows the Working Sessions deck (Blocks 1 to 4). Blocks 2 and 3 build on persona v1 from the persona workshop (#8), the interviews and the pre-read comments. No earlier personas exist, so show how each persona was built and mark thin evidence on the cards.

The reference vote (4.1) and the card sort (4.4) sit inside the Design block: the vote sets the look and feel before sketching, the card sort turns the sketches into a navigation structure. Both feed the IA and Branding deliverables.
Card sort with 10 to 12 people is directional. Photograph each group’s result and test the IA again in usability round 1.
Keep references to examples HT may see; check permissions and remove pricing before printing.
Evening (Slalom only): transcribe boards, write the Day 1 playback, start prototype v0 and prepare Day 2.

WS.title: Design session, Day 2 (#13): commit to a prioritised backlog
meta: HT: 4 to 6 stakeholders, Product Owner, Programme Owner signs
WS.goal: Refine the concept and scope, shape epics and user stories, rank and sequence the backlog, and leave with a signed-off backlog, a first change and adoption plan and next steps. Phases: Refine, Prioritise, Commit.
rows: Slalom replays the concept and decisions from Day 1. Each HT participant adds one reaction on a sticky note: keep, change or worry
Group the notes and the Day 1 parking lot into themes. Small groups take one theme each and report back with a proposed answer

Plenary with a simple in, out, later board. Agree what the concept covers for the first release and what waits. Tag each item standard or tailored as it is placed (replaces a separate customization exercise)
Updated concept, scope boundary, light standard-or-tailored view
Affinity grouping. Teams cluster the Must and Should requirements from Day 1 into epics, each tied to a journey moment
Story workshop in mixed groups using “As a [employee], I want… so that…”. The Solution Architect checks feasibility as stories take shape
Draft user stories with acceptance notes
Walk the backlog against the success measures and personas. Spot gaps, duplicates and stories no one can explain
2x2 wall exercise. HT stakeholders place each epic by employee value; the Solution Architect adds a first view of effort and complexity
Story-map slicing. Groups cut the map into a first release and later releases, keeping each slice useful to employees on its own
Pre-mortem: “It is launch day and it went badly. Why?” Capture risks and dependencies that could change the sequence
Stakeholder and impact mapping. Who is affected, what changes for them, and what support the first release needs (communications, training, Champions)
Change and adoption plan, first draft
Structured walk-through of the ranked backlog with fist-of-five consent. Concerns are captured and resolved in the room or given an owner. Programme Owner signs
Round-robin check-out. Agree next steps, owners and dates (including prototype scope and the usability test tasks for Thu 19 Nov), review the parking lot, capture what worked and what to change
Next steps with owners and dates
tips: Agenda follows the Working Sessions deck (Blocks 5 to 8). Log every decision the same day and share it by evening.
If stakeholders disagree on a priority or on standard versus tailored, record both positions rather than forcing consensus.
Confirm early who from HT can approve the backlog; the Programme Owner signs in Block 8.
Anything new after sign-off goes through change control.

WS.title: Usability testing, rounds 1 and 2 (#17, #20)
WS.goal: Find the biggest usability problems before Design sign-off.
rows: Explain it tests the design, not them; recording and notes
Typical day or shift, tools they use, last time they needed information

Ease rating 1 to 7 per task; what surprised you; what they would change

How they get information today, what they need at the start of a shift, languages, device access
Site interviews via the Change Lead, supervisors, #8
Team leader or plant manager
The main way information reaches the frontline; short on time.
What they relay, how, and what they need from HR and comms
Group B interviews, #8
Desk employee
Uses email and Teams; wants to find policies, people and news quickly.
Top tasks, search and navigation pain points, what they use instead of the intranet
Group C interviews, #7, usability round 1
Remote or hybrid employee
Relies on digital channels and may feel disconnected from sites.
What keeps them connected, which tools, time zones and languages
Group D interviews, #8
New starter
Needs onboarding information and the right people in one place.
The first 30 days: questions, who they ask, what is missing
Group E interviews, HR input
Content owner or department rep
Publishes for a team or site; skills vary widely.
What they publish, how often, what help and templates they need
Group F interviews, #16 content assessment
JRN: Frontline staff start with a supervisor briefing or a noticeboard, not a digital channel.
People ask a colleague or HR first because search and navigation do not lead them to the right document.
Desk employee, team leader, content owner
Employees do not know whom to ask, so requests go to a supervisor or HR by phone or email.
Frontline hears news late and second-hand; desk staff see it by email or Teams.
Employees raise concerns informally to a supervisor; a digital route would need anonymity and works council agreement.
Recognition happens locally and is not visible beyond the team.
New starters get information in pieces from several people, in different languages.
